controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body color at its measured dayside temperature, 1,535 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of WASP-94 A b's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 3.6 µm (Spitzer IRAC). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

controls.label: Climate model
controls.qualification: Simulation · Met Office UM · Mukherjee et al. (2025) · False color
controls.notes: Temperature at 1 millibar of WASP-94 A b in the Met Office UM simulation of Mukherjee et al. (2025): a model, not a measurement. The run assumes a hydrogen and helium atmosphere with the Sun's share of heavier elements and no clouds, on a planet that turns once for each orbit. The map is one instant, the last state the release holds, read where the pressure is 1 millibar. With JWST, Mukherjee et al. (2025) measured the evening edge 449 ± 83 K hotter than the morning edge; in this model it is about 300 K hotter at this pressure. Gray caps: no released grid samples beyond 89° north or south. The false color runs from 900 to 1,700 K; it is not what an eye would see. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: The orbits of WASP-94 A's planets in this map from above, to scale, with WASP-94 A b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

WASP-94 A b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (68, 95, 105) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 92352620, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 18-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
